utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I noticed where most of the laptops seem to be functioning, Judge Nieto-Navia has nothing on his laptop screen. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I was informed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that you wanted to address the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In fact, Mr. President, yes. I'd like to say that my laptop apparently refuses to work, so if we could have the assistance of a technician, I would be grateful. The reason for which -- I can continue in this manner. The reason for which I wanted to address your Trial Chamber, Mr. President, is that yesterday we heard in this courtroom words that surprised Defence counsel and perhaps others too. We heard the Prosecution affirm in front of the witness using the traditional formula, of course, I put to you that, I suggest that, they told him that he was guilty of a crime, that is to say that he perhaps participated in a crime. That he participated in intentional fire on civilians. In many legal systems when a magistrate or a legal officer is here, regardless of his position, when someone affirms such a thing in public this is considered to be a serious matter and there are two possibilities that seem to arise. Either one instigates proceeding against this person. We know that you committed such-and-such an act and we are go to proceed because we are prosecuting -- we are accusing you or this is not done and then a minimal restraint should be applied everyone should know that, both sides should know that. And this would be observed in such situations. When such a thing is affirmed, even if it is true that the Rule 90(H) tries to get the witness to contradict such an affirmation in the course of a cross-examination when such a thing is affirmed one goes too far. The threshold is crossed, a threshold is crossed which should not be crossed. And in addition one attempts in this manner to destabilise the witness and I don't think that this is acceptable. All the more so, in that on one occasion, the Defence used the word "lie" with regard to a witness and we were admonished by the Trial Chamber and we were told that it wasn't good, it wasn't necessary to use language that was too strong with regard to such proceedings. So when one claims that a witness has committed a crime, that he personally has committed a crime in public, Defence counsel considers this to be unacceptable and that such behaviour should quite simply be sanctioned. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, any need to respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the remarks by my learned colleague indicate a failure on his part to understand the requirements of Rule 90(H). The witness's evidence made it necessary and unavoidable for the Prosecution to put that proposition to him. In particular the witness said that except for time off duty during which he slept at Mrkovici, he was on that part of the front line for the duration of the war, therefore, including the indictment period, he and 14 -- up to 14 fellow soldiers. The Prosecution case is that two of the scheduled sniping victims were shot from that ridge, therefore, squarely, either he or one or more of his fellow 14 soldiers were responsible. Rule 90(H) requires the Prosecution to, out of fairness if nothing else to put to him that either he or his fellow soldiers were engaged in that activity, not only in relation to the two scheduled incidents, but they are illustrations. There is other evidence of sniping of civilians in that area which the Prosecution says was done deliberately or indiscriminately. So the witness having squarely placed himself in that area of responsibility, it was necessary to put to him that, firstly, he or his fellows were responsible, and secondly, they received orders, the effect of which was to target civilians. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you said that the behaviour should be sanctioned. The Chamber will consider having heard you and the response of Mr. Ierace whether there is a reason to take action upon your request. We will consider that, not at this very moment, but we will consider that in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'd like to add that when I say that such behaviour should be penalised, where it is a manner of speaking, I wouldn't want you to understand to take this to mean that I want anyone to be penalised. When I say that it should be penalised, what I want to say is that such behaviour should not be accepted. That's what I wanted to say. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and I think that what I intended to say is not to fine or send Mr. Ierace to gaol for it, but I had in mind that the Chamber would express itself on the appropriateness of the way Mr. Ierace questioned the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps I should add that what I did would not only be expected of me in a common law trial, but I would attract disapproval if I did not do that, if I did not put to a witness, who, by his evidence, placed himself in that position of responsibility that he was responsible and that those orders were given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I think, but if I am wrong in my understanding please tell me so that we can take that into consideration when considering the matter put to us by Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that what you did is part of what you think the Defence should have done at many occasions when the Prosecution witnesses were examined. Is that a correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: One example is General Karavelic, at the end of his cross-examination, I pointed out that it had not been put to him that he was responsible for firing on civilians on the ABiH side. That is just one example. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will consider the matter. Before the Defence will call its next witness, I'd first like to turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And may I then take it, Ms. Pilipovic, that the Defence is [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, would you please --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague will start with the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we have forgotten one thing. We first should deal with the documents that -- I made a mistake. I mentioned the name of the witness in open session. So a redaction should be made. I apologise for the inconvenience caused by me. But before we call the next witness, Madam Registrar, could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then since the correction is repaired, we could go through the documents of yesterday introduced by the witness, Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1794, map marked by witness; Exhibit D338, photograph; Exhibit P3756, photograph marked by witness; Exhibit P3763, Exhibit P3757, Exhibit P3762, Exhibit P3758, Exhibit P3760, all photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These documents are admitted into evidence since I hear no objections. Ms. Pilipovic, since for the next witness there is no application for protective measures, I would like to know what will be the pseudonym you will use.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, DP53.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pilipovic. Then, Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP53, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will not use your name since protective measures are effective in respect of you. Mr. DP53, before giving evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The next of this declaration will be handed out to you now by the usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will first be examined by counsel for the Defence. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, since you are standing, I take it that you will start.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think I received the French translation, but I don't think that is very important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, good day. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, now I am going to show you a sheet of paper, first of all, and could you just answer the following question by saying yes or no: What is written -- can you tell us whether what is written on this piece of paper is exact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The usher can take away the sheet of paper. Mr. President, we could perhaps go into closed session, closed session or private session, but I think that closed session would be better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there is no one in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, I leave it to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us what you did between spring 1992 and winter 1993, which is the period that corresponds to the period of hostilities? And for the sake of the transcript, and it was well transcribed in Serb, 1995, which still does not appear in the transcript. There it is. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: I apologise. Could you repeat that question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do between spring 1992, 9-2, and winter 1995, 9-5, that is to say during the period of hostilities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, I was engaged in the defence of my property and my family house in Mrkovici. I was involved in this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you part of a company of any kind, of a military group at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes. At the beginning when the conflict first broke out we had organised the defence ourselves, and afterwards, once the Army of Republika Srpska had been established --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will stop you there. I apologise. You said that you had organised defence yourself. Can you briefly tell us how this took place, how this was done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: On the 6th of April, since the relations between the national parties were very tense, and guards had been formed before the conflict itself broke out, that was in fact the reserve police officer. It was the department in Mrkovici. They controlled unknown people who would Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. come to that territory. And on the 6th of April 1992 or rather on the 5th of April 1992, in the course of one such control provoked from firearms. And then we, the inhabitants of that village, went out to see what was happening. And on the 6th of April, a neighbour and relatives were killed just below the so-called Mala Kula in Mrkovici, which is where our neighbour's property is located, neighbour's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I am now going to return to my previous question. You told us that you had organised yourself. At the very beginning what arms did you have at your disposal, and I am referring to the very beginning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well at the very beginning we had the weapons that the reserve police officer had, the weapons of that group that was there. There were about eight or nine men there. And it was in the school in Mrkovici they were armed by the police officer at the time. They had automatic and semi-automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, after you had started organising yourselves, what happened, that is to say, after May, June 1992, were you organised in a different way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, after that event on the 6th of April a number of us went to control those people who were coming to our village and who would pass through our village. So we were more involved and engaged at the -- at the boundaries which were at the end of the village in the direction of Sarajevo, at the bottom of the village. And later on we were organised as the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. When you intervened, when you were part of the Army of Republika Srpska in what capacity did you serve in that army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: I was a private, an ordinary soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. What arm of the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: There is no interpretation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't have interpretation either. In which arm, in which branch of the army, for instance, we know the air force, the navy, which...?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No infantry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Mrkovici, Mrkovici was an infantry company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So, Witness, can you tell us where exactly, if that was the case, you were stationed and for how long and during which period of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: We were stationed in the sector from the so-called Mala Kula and to the Velika Kula, large fort, and that was throughout the time of the war operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us where the large fort is or the large tower, where was it, that is the Velika Kula?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: That was on the north-east side of Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How far is that facility from what we call -- the facility that we call Mala Kula?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Two and a half kilometers, approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And between these two facilities what was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Between these two there is an important elevation point, Spicasta Stijena, sharpstone feature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. How long were you there in this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: In the area of responsibility of the company, I spent the entire war there except occasionally when I was wounded and when I was on leave, on sickness leave for treatment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You tell us that you spent the entire war there, Witness, but were there not moments of rest, of leave, that men from the front would be relieved; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: That would just be temporary for a few hours, for purposes of rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Of course. But when this rest was taken, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: I would go to my house in Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Throughout the period of the war, Witness, how many times were you able to go back to your house and I am not asking you to give us a precise number, but was it rare? Was it frequent? How often?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: That depended on the situation on the line itself. For instance, if there were some important considerable operation against us, then rarely, and if there was not so intense, then it would be every five or six days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on average, five or six days you would go back to the same place; is that correct? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, we will come back to the situation, to your situation on the line at Spicasta Stijena, but at the moment I'd like you to tell us about the weapons of the opposing side. First of all, would you be able to tell us, yes or no, about the weapons of the opposing side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What is your personal experience of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, they had infantry weapons and artillery weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What artillery weapons were you able to see yourself with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Mortars, and a couple of times I saw a tank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you able to see a tank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, we saw the tank in the area of the transmitter on Hum, and in the area of the Ciglana tunnel from where it fired in the direction of our positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your positions, was it possible to see the area of Ciglana and the area of the Hum hill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, on the right-hand side of our lines it was possible to see that part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the name of that area that you said was to the right? Does it have a name, a specific name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: That is right from Mala Kula and that is called Orlovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that you saw a tank on Hum and one tank in Ciglana. Was this the same tank or were there two different tanks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: I don't know that because it didn't happen at the same time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you please approach the microphone, Witness. Just a little bit more. Thank you. Or perhaps you could just approach the microphone towards you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please assist the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke to us also about the mortar. But do you know what were the calibres that were used by the opposing side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: As far as the calibres concerned, they used all calibres of mortars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that means?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: 60, 82, and 120-millimetres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. To the extent that you were able to have the view of that side of Sarajevo, do you know where were these mortar batteries of the opposing side of the enemy deployed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: In certain periods of time I do know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: In 1992, 1993, and so on. And so on. Except that mortar is a mobile weapon so if it is found by the other side, then it would be moved to the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But could you tell us where did you see these mortars or where did you know that they were located in this period, in 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, according to the reports from intelligence services, we had information that mortars were located 82-millimetre calibre in the area of Sedrenik near Karavdina Kuca, so-called Karavda house, and the 120 millimetre mortar and the 82-millimetre by the cemetery Bare, and the 120 by the Kosevo Hospital in the area of the engineering faculty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you repeat the name of the house which was not recorded in the transcript where one 82 and 120-millimetre calibre Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. mortars was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Karavdina Kuca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it have a different name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No, that was his last name, the last name of the owner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I am going to come back to what you told us. You told us about an area which is near the Kosevo Hospital, and you also told us about the Bare cemetery. Where is cemetery Bare located, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: It is located on the western side of the Kosevo Hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. At which distance, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: As the crow flies 300 to 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The same question for the technical faculty -- I see there is a problem in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether it is a problem in the transcript, but you asked at what distance. It is not clear at what distance from where, from where the witness was or from the Kosevo Hospital, 300 to 400 metres from where, Mr. DP53?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From Kosevo Hospital. From Kosevo Hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the same question from the Kosevo Hospital how far was the engineering faculty or the technical faculty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: 100 meters, but not as the crow flies, but on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, do you know according to your personal experience, the opposing side had other heavy weapons. You spoke to us and I will remind you, about the mortars and tanks. Were there any other weapons that were used against you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: They had a lot of weapons. They had Browning guns that from which the fire was opened on us very frequently. They had other artillery weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What other weapons, what other pieces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: I am not an expert in large-calibre weapons, but they were probably Howitzers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could -- with the assistance of Mr. Usher, Madam Registrar, could we have the map that we usually have a look at, which is map in relation to incident number 3 and 8. We have one copy in colour for the witness for the ELMO. And for the others a black and white copy. Thank you. And with your leave, Mr. President, perhaps Mr. Usher could place the map on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... 1796.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we thank Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise, more or less, what is depicted on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: More or less, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you say more or less?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: I can't quite work it out, whether it has been slightly enlarged or what. I can try.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, try and position or to locate on this map, if you can, the location where -- the location that you called Velika Kula, the large fort. First of all, could you please point to it with the pointer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: It is about here somewhere, but there is -- I think that's missing, that part is missing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please take a black pen and put a black cross on the upper border of the map where you were pointing. And if you can write next to it initials "VK."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. On this map you can see an upper line, upper line which is dark green and below it a wavy light green line. Now, the dark green line is supposed to represent the position of the VRS positions at the time of the conflict. Bearing in mind the modifications that you can also see --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am just -- I was informed, that the witness, when he is leaning over, that causes sometimes some problems. But please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please not lean over too much. Yes, thank you very much. Could you please indicate if the position of these lines appear to you to be more or less confirmed with reality or perhaps something else should be modified? And I am talking about the VRS line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: I think it should be modified.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Shall I draw --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please point first with the pointer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, please give the witness the pointer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Witness, could you please do the same thing now with a black pen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I would be grateful if you can just go over this line just to make it a little darker, please, with the pen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, could you now focus on the lower part, that is the area to the south of -- that is of the lighter line. This lighter line represents the positions of the opposing army, that is of the BH Army. Do you know if there was just one line of Defence or were there more?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I might have missed it but perhaps it would be clear if we knew the period that he was talking about. Was that the entire period or a particular part of the period?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps this could be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will ask the question. Yes, gladly. I will ask the question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the line that you just drew was this a line that changed or does it correspond to one period in the conflict, specifically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: This is the line which remained unchanged except for certain trenches. For instance, Mala Kula and sharpstone feature that fell several times into the hands of the opponent and were then returned again to our area of responsibility. But basically this was the line that remained throughout the war, didn't change, except for some parts that in case that they attacked, then they would fall into their hands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, I am going to ask you the same question in relation to the lines of the other side, of the opposing side, and that is for the entire period. Was there one single system of lines or was there several lines, a system of multiple lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: There were several systems of lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you be able to draw these lines? Could you do it, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Do you mean the opposing army or?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the opposing side in fact, but could you please use the pointer, please. Show us what you mean.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: I think this line isn't correctly drawn in because this elevation 906 was held by the opposing side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Witness, if the light green line seems incorrectly positioned on the map I would be very grateful if you could correct it with the black pen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would a double line be a good suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Mr. President. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we are speaking about the lower line, that is the light green line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: They ran parallel to each other, more or less, but this map seems slightly enlarged to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Don't worry about the map and its problems.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And more to the right, Witness, how would that go, if you are able to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I am assuming that you drew here the first line of defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now draw the second and then the third.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I would be grateful if in the future the meaning of the witness's evidence is not assumed what he could be asking a leading question about it. Just in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you refrain from leading, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked the question whether there were several lines and I think your answer was that there were several lines, is that correct, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How many lines were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, there were three lines of defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know, more or less, the situation on the ground of these three lines, the location of these three lines on the ground? Could you please -- Witness, could you please answer? Did you know more or less --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Not in all areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you please draw the part that you knew.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: In some areas --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just draw the lines that you knew, the areas of the lines that you knew.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you do it, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when you finish this line, I would be grateful if that is the case to put a number "2" next to it, if that is number "2."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we could leave it as a dotted line and not make it a -- well, Mr. DP53, I am afraid it is too late now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So that is number 2, represents the second line. And could you please draw the 3rd line, still as a dotted line, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please put number "3" next to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the very first line that you drew, could you please put number "1" and then things will be in order. The first line of defence of the forces --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I wondered whether the first line of the BiH forces and I take it now that the witness has put two "1s" and he crosses out one of them now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, here it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First line of the BiH forces. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness. With the assistance of Mr. Usher, could we please make it larger, the view larger and if you can take the pointer into your hand. Thank you. Now, if we can just go -- if we can zoom out, rather. Thank you very much. Just a little bit more. Just a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you point out to us on this map, if you can, the view you had at the time of the war, the view of Sedrenik and perhaps of other places, but indicate on this map the view that you could have had from your positions, and namely, towards the south, in the south, southern part of the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Which part are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, exactly, that's it. Show us on the map the part that you could see and the part that you couldn't see, as a result.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which part could you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: The parts to the right of me could be seen, but not the parts to the left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Could you take a marker. In order to facilitate the exercise, we have a ruler that might be helpful. Thank you. Could you do that again, but could you draw a line now with a black felt tip.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. And if I have understood you correctly, the right part that is to say the part that is to the east on this map, is the part that you could see and the other part is the part that you couldn't see; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, why were you not able to see the other part, the part which is to the west in the map or south-west?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, we couldn't see that part because the parts of the lines that could perhaps be seen were in front of us. There was a forest there. And the observation post that we had here, it was also not possible to see that part from the post, that other part, because the observation post wasn't on the edge of the terrain. It was a little further back from the ridge, from the edge. And this part here in front of the line, well, in fact, there was a forest in front of us. It was a forested area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, would it have been possible to have a better view if one were on the peak of the ridge, on the top of the ridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Not in wartime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why not, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, because one would have been hit by enemy fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, it might be a bit confusing. May I ask you: You have drawn a line from a red circle to approximately where the "3" is. You first indicated that you had a view on what is on the right-hand side of that line. Then you later told us that you had no view on what was on the left-hand side of that line. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, from my right side, this part could be seen, and this part here, couldn't be seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But then you added later on that you couldn't see the other part either, so which was a bit confusing for me. But, could you please perhaps indicate what part you could see, for example, by --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Beside the number "3" maybe?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you could see whatever was on the map on the right-hand side of the line you have drawn from north-west to south-east. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, at the bottom of this map a place called Bakija can be seen. You have the word Bakija, can you see it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what there was in that area as far as military installations are concerned, possible military installations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: In this area where it says "Bakija" there was a cemetery and the barracks of the former Yugoslav Army was next to the cemetery. And where it says Streliste and it has been underlined here, I think that's where the facilities are located.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you point to -- yes, but could you pull your head back, please, so that we can see this -- could you point out the area that you referred to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: This is where the barracks of the former Yugoslav Army was located.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would be grateful if you could draw circle around this area, using a black felt tip. Draw a circle around it, please, around the barracks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you write "K" next to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, can you see a point bearing the number "3"? Can you see the number 3 on the map? No, a dot. Thank you. Can you see it? No, it is further to the left. No. Below.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. As far as you can remember what is the distance, because we are talking about a diagonal, what is the distance between the barracks that you mentioned and this point, point number 3, if you can tell us, as the crow flies? Between point number 3 and the barracks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, about -- between 200 and 300 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, could you do the same for point 8, if you can find it on the map. Can you find a second red dot which is further to the north. Not the number, the dot.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'd like to ask you the same question with regard to the distance between the barracks and the red dot, as far as you can remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: I think it was about 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I would now like you to show us on this map, if you can -- I will withdraw that and I will reformulate my question. Was there any shooting at your positions from Sedrenik; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, can you tell us, and use the pointer, from which area was fire opened at your lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, they opened fire from infantry weapons and from points along the entire line. And from heavy weapons, from the barracks, they opened fire from a Browning and they fired from mortars from this area, which is somewhere here above the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Could you please take a marker and make a cross at the site that you have pointed out with the pointer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's good. You were just above the red rectangle. That's where you were a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what this place is called, do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, this is the location of what I mentioned a minute ago, Karavdina Kuca, but this place here is called Streliste, it's a wider area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please write two "KKs" next to the cross that you have made, and this will mark the house concerned.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now could you make a cross next to the shooting ground that you mentioned a minute ago -- no. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you write the letter "P" next to this facility.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, thank you. Next to these facilities that you have just marked "P" and "K and K" were there military positions of any kind next to these facilities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Before the conflict broke out, the Streliste was here too. The Streliste, the shooting ground that belonged to the former Yugoslav Army and to the Territorial Defence. It was a shooting ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I am referring to the period of the conflict, from spring 1992 to winter 1995, the period that you were familiar with. At these two facilities, "P" and "KK," were there any military forces at these sites?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, as far as we knew the place marked with the letter "K" 82-millimetre mortar were positioned there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: And there were lines up near Visoko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the direction of near the site marked with the letter P, were there any troops positioned there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, could you now point out with the pointer, but could we enlarge the map so that we can see the upper and the lower parts of the map. Witness, when there were exchanges of fire between the two sides, could you outline by using the pointer the direction of fire from the entire line that you pointed out a minute ago, the green line, the line towards the east?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, towards the lines of the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you carry on, outline the line on the entire map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness rapidly outlined six or five lines going in the direction of the south-east in general and in the direction of the Bakija zone and the zones that he indicated a minute ago as "P" and "K and K." I think we can remove the map, now and place the exhibits that were admitted as evidence a minute ago, we could place these exhibits on the ELMO. 3756P, and -- no, I apologise. 3758 and 3760. It is a 360-degree photograph [as interpreted]. It is a panoramic picture of Sarajevo it consists of two parts, and I will show it to you so that you can see what photograph is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indicated to me what number that is?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will repeat it, gladly. It is Exhibit 3758 and 3760, "P" for Prosecution. If the usher could superimpose these photographs. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There has been an error in the transcript where it says that it is a 360-degrees photograph, I think you said it was an overlapping photograph. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Mr. President, but I think I said panoramic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, my first question, can you see any minarets in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you indicate some of them with a pointer so that we are clear about what you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness showed between 8 and 10 buildings in this photograph, both to the left and to the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you ever have the opportunity of seeing the area that was photographed, that is photographed, immediately after the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. During your stay there, that is to say during the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. war, any of the minarets that you have pointed to and that you could have seen from your positions, had any of these minarets been destroyed by fire coming from your lines or coming from your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: None of them could have been destroyed because our company didn't have any heavy weapons and infantry weapons can't --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Witness, since we have this photograph on the screen could you place your pointer in the left area, the upper left-hand area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Further to the right, please. A little lower down. Further to the right. Towards the big building that we can see. Further.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Stop there. Do you know what this building is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Just a minute. That was also the barracks of the former Yugoslavia, it was called Jajce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness pointed, for the sake of the transcript, to a large building located in the upper part of the photograph number 3758. It is the upper third, it is of ocher colour, as far as the walls are concerned and the roof appears to be brown.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what is the building in front of these barracks and which is on a small hill? Can you see it? And it appears that we can see stellas there. Further down. Further down.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stop, stop. What is this building that we can see which is apparently on a plateau?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Here?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. It is a building which appears to be horizontal. No, it is not a building, for the translation, it is a feature. Can you see a sort of field with white tombstones. It is below. Below. Below. Over there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. To the right. Stop.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stop. What can you see here, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: It is a cemetery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it a cemetery which is near the barracks that you mentioned a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No. It is -- the barracks that I mentioned a minute ago is located here behind this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we enlarge the photograph some more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you do that again. Could you point that again, please, Witness, where was the barracks? Where were the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: The barracks were behind this cemetery here. You can't see it here in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness pointed to the left side, the left edge, the upper third of photograph 3758 and stated that there was a cemetery there that could be made out and the barracks in question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, before the break I would like you to do the following: If the usher gives you a blank sheet of paper, could you take this blank sheet of paper and after the usher has joined the two photographs --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you use the blank sheet of paper that you have been given to show the view you had from your positions, that is to say, from the forward observation post, indicate what you could see during the war, and could you conceal what you couldn't see.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that this is the time for a break. We can leave things as they are and we will carry on if you like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I -- yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have done the following: We have prepared the same photographs in black and white. We will do the same exercise and mark them again so as to save time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I would rather have in the transcript as well what happened until now. And it is the cemetery the witness pointed at which was not near to the barracks is on photograph P3758, approximately halfway up a little bit left from the centre where we see a lot of tiny little white objects, as it seems to be. And where the witness did put a virgin piece of paper over the two photographs he was covering almost the whole of the right photograph, and a large upper part of the photograph on the left. We will adjourn until 20 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Before we continue, one observation for the parties. We talked about whether we would sit in December on the 2nd, on the 3rd. The 2nd was not a day on which we would sit. The 3rd, there have been plans to change the Plenary to the 3rd. These plans have been chanced now. So we will sit on the 3rd. The Plenary will be on the 12th and the 13th. So, therefore, the 11th which was not scheduled for sitting becomes available. I still hope to hear soon from General Galic how his family visit has been planned, but the 11th might be a day where we could sit. This is not a proposal. This is not a decision. But just to inform the parties as I promised you to keep you informed as good as I could and as quickly as I could. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just wish to inform you that the 11th is suitable for us. The family of General Galic is coming to visit on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So then please, could the parties prepare, as I said, it is not yet a decision. We still have to consider it, but at least take into consideration that we might sit on the 11th. Then Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Ms. Pilipovic was also speaking my name. I will also be present if we have to work on the 11th. Perhaps now we could distribute with the assistance of Mr. Usher, the black and white copies, those are the exact copies of the two photographs, but we are going to give them a number. And I am going to give the instructions to the witness. What I'd like to do is for him to do the same exercise again that he did on the two photographs, once they have been gathered or rather joined together by Mr. Usher. And if he can draw with a black pen the zone that was not visible for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could Mr. Usher join the two photographs --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- shown to the witness. I have been shown D1797, and D17 -- well, they are both marked D1797.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I made a change to one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay, one should be D1798. And there seems to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there seems to be markings on them. May I take it that these markings might not be a real objection. It is about what you called yesterday "an important question" I take it, Mr. Piletta-Zanin? You asked yesterday a question and you were a bit worried that you could not put that question to the witness. You said that it was very important. Is it clear that what we find markings on this map is the subject of that question from yesterday. A similar question was put to the witness today I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which markings are we speaking about, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The small circles on it. Many, many, many.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, Mr. President, I apologise. These circles have nothing to do with anything and I wanted to ask the witness not to pay any attention to them. Just not to pay any attention to them. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think it would not cause any problem. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please do the same exercise again, just like before. Could you place a blank sheet of paper -- if you don't have it, you will be handed one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please position this piece of paper again. I think that you are showing us here the part that you did not see; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, if you can, because we can't see it on the screen. Here it is now. Could you please now draw a line along the sheet of paper on the both photographs, please. You can perhaps take a ruler and draw a line. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that the line should be visible on the photographs. Yes, it is visible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Witness, I'd be grateful if you can shade out the part that you couldn't see.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These two photographs can be removed now from the ELMO. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, can we speak about the frequency of fighting. The photographs we no longer need them. They can be removed. When we spoke about the fighting, I would like to speak about the frequency of fighting, what was the frequency of fighting? And I am talking about the rhythm of the exchanges of fire and how considerable they were, what was their intensity of the exchanges of fire, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Fighting went on a daily basis. Speaking of intensity, occasionally there were just acts of provocation and very often every few days there were more -- there was more intense fighting. On average every 10 days or so there would be more intense attacks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you say they were much more intense, what kind of exchange of fire are we talking about? What type of weapons that was used then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Most of the time it was infantry weapons that were used and in these considerable high intensity exchanges of fire was used also artillery and mortars, Browning guns and recoilless cannons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You are talking about infantry weapons. What was your gun that you used, your rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, what was the range, and I am not talking about the killing range, but I am talking about the theoretical range of such a weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: The range was up to about 800 metres. And the shooting is done up to 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "800 metres" is that starting from 800 metres, the bullets stops, does it go into the ground, fall to the ground?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, could you now please describe the situation regarding the uniforms. First of all, in 1992 and 1993, what was the situation on -- for you personally? Did you have a uniform at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: In 1992 we didn't have uniforms, but we were in civilian clothes and spent practically the entire year, except for individuals who managed somehow to get some parts of uniform. But the uniform we didn't have, but we were in civilian clothes, with some details. Perhaps a cap or a part of a uniform, whatever anyone could lay their hands on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. For 1992 and for 1993, as far as uniform was concerned, what was the situation among the opposing forces, the enemy forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Very similar, the same. They couldn't get uniforms either. They also had all kinds of parts of uniforms. Some people had uniforms of the reserve police force. Most people would have some vestige of uniform with civilian parts of clothing as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us what was the colour of the uniforms used by the enemy from the moment when the enemy started using uniforms, and if there are different colours, can you tell us which ones they are, which ones they were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: These were what we called camouflage uniforms, dark green colour or black-green colour. And then also of the reserve police force uniforms which is blue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see with your own eyes such uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What I mean is both the leopard-type uniforms the black-green uniforms and the blue uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. These uniforms, were they worn indistinctly by the persons who were attacking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The witness seems to understand the question but perhaps it could be clarified so we know what the answer relates to.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I am going to rephrase this question in a different way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when the attacks took place, the enemies, did they -- the enemy, did they wear uniforms occasionally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: They wore uniforms after the 1993, but before in 1992 only individuals had uniforms. It was later on that everybody had uniforms after 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am talking about the persons who wore uniforms or parts of uniform in 1993. Did you see them, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: In 1993, a majority had uniforms, camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Did you also see in 1993 blue uniforms that were worn by the men, persons, soldiers, attacking, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. What kind of uniforms were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: These were the uniforms of the reserve police force, it is just like a soldiers uniforms except that it is blue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Specifically, since you are talking about the police force, do you know if the police force was also engaged and deployed in combat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Very frequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: We know that because in cases of attack we also saw the blue uniforms and the green camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the police forces were the only ones that had blue uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there paramilitary units in the area of Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: In the start of the war when the conflict broke out before the war started, we were stopped by some kind of reserve police, but in fact these were paramilitary units. And they were checking the area before the conflict broke out, and after the conflict broke out, we didn't even go down there any more. They were checking the vehicles, they were checking the IDs and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the colour of their uniforms or the colour or the colours of their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Blue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: With caps. They called berets, the so-called Green Berets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the ELMO, could we have the P3756 so that the witness can answer some other questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, so that we can all find our bearings, very rapidly, could you please point where was what you called Mala Kula, a small fort?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: It is here, but you can't see it very well because of the aerial here. You can just see the top of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness points to a hill which is to the left of the photograph just at the foot below what looks like to be an electrical aerial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, to the right of the location that you pointed to, that is middle of the photograph you see a ridge. Can you please point to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: This here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What is its name, the name of that ridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: It is called Spicasta Stijena, sharpstone feature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. At the foot of that ridge we see a kind of brown area in the -- below the pine trees. Can you please indicate, point, that above the road --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness is pointing to a brownish area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: These were trenches that were used by the opposing forces. That is their first line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this the first line that you earlier drew on the map, on the plan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Between your lines that we believe that they are on the top part of the hill, and this point here, what is the nature of the terrain? What is the slope of the terrain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Below our line there is a slope. It goes downwards. And as you can see it on the photograph it goes up and then it goes much more steeply downwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this explain what we can see on the map, that the lines are very near, although the distance can be a lot greater when we bear in mind the steepness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, could you please show with your pointer a group of houses that represented the defence lines facing your positions? Could you point to them, please, on the plateau of Sedrenik, the valley of Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: There were several lines here. This was the first line here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do it very slowly. The second one.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Here. That's the first line going here, this way. And here you can see a trench, a communicating tunnel for trenches --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Stop there. Leave the pointer. Don't move it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. No. Yes. Leave it there. Don't move it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness drew a line which goes below the little fort towards the wood, goes down the slope and then joins just above the road we see on the photograph, the communicating trenches, the trenches that we see just below the trees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, to the right of your pointer there is a group of houses. Can you see? Below. Below.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness points to the group of the houses below to the right of the road, right in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what did these houses represent in terms of a defence? What were these houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: In terms of the defence these houses represented the second line of defence. On this photograph you can also see the communicating trenches. This is where their second line was set up. And here, between the houses. There were also communicating trenches that were dug up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, the witness is indicating two groups of houses. The first one is more to the centre to the right of the photograph, and the second one is more in the upper part, slightly diagonally to the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the photograph that you saw earlier, this double photograph that you had a look at, in your opinion, from which location could it have been taken, that is the view that we had on the two photographs earlier, in your opinion, from where could it have been taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: This photograph could have been taken about here --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Don't move your pointer. Don't move your pointer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is pointing approximately below an object which is white and red, which we think are houses. And this is the part corresponding to the upper third of the ridge near a slightly whitish area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, as far as the 906 elevation, you said that this was under the control of the enemy. Where is, in your opinion, 906 elevation point located on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Here. It is located here, just behind the aerial, this aerial here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness points approximately on the electric aerial which is on the top of the hill to the left of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, here. On the top. The elevation point is always top of something, like a hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the distance between this point and the fort that you had under your control called Mala Kula, the little fort, the small fort?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: About 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This photograph can be removed from the screen. Could we please have photograph 3760. And in the meantime, I am going to ask the witness other questions regarding fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find yourself personally in a situation of fighting when considerable attacks were launched by the enemy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes, very frequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you give us some dates of considerable enemy attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: These large-scale attacks were very frequent. And that depended on which period we are talking about. There were many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. If we talk about spring 1993, summer 1993, what was the situation there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Spring of 1993 I know that they had taken, during an attack, sharpstone feature from us, that is one trench which we called Kristine [phoen] because there were three trenches on the sharpstone feature. And this last trench next to Mala Kula ran there and it was taken from us at the end of -- spring, it was April, end of April 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you say that you lost sharpstone feature, do you mean that you lost the elevations as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: We just lost that one trench on the sharpstone feature. That is just one part of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please show that on the photograph -- no, the other photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at this photograph later. Thank you. The previous one which is 3756, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Can I please have something a little thinner because I think on this photograph this pointer would represent some 50 metres or something. Here. Here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, please don't mark it. Don't write anything, please. I am sorry, I am just trying to make it easier for you to a point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please approach me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what you are currently indicating with the white pointer, it's what you lost or what you were able to defend?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: That's what in April 1993 we lost this part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is pointing to the right border of the whitish area which is on top of the ridge, saying that this was what was lost in April --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which year? Which year, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: 1993. And after that there were a couple of other occasions too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was just checking for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you lost this facility, I think you spoke about April 1993, was that the first half of April or the second half of April 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: In the second half of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
