utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, when you said "to the right border of the whitish area" did you intend to say the left border or? Where the witness now is pointing I would consider to be the right part of the whitish area, and where he pointed at was rather in the upper left corner. Would you agree? Where he is pointing at now, you described that as the right corner. I would rather think of it as the left corner, the left upper corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please show again with your pointer so that we can see exactly where you are pointing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is pointing to -- thank you -- to two facilities -- perhaps if you could move your hand. I know it is not easy. Here it is. Thank you. On two facilities that are to the left of the pointer and they seem to us to be two facilities either walls or houses.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. But these two facilities are at a distance from this point here. But it just seems that they are close to each other. But between this point and these two facilities, these two houses, is 200 metres. It just looks closer on the photograph. Between this point and these two facilities, there is some 200 metres. Because the way the terrain is laid out, that's what it looks like.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, in the days that followed the loss of these facilities, were there -- was there intense fighting in order to retake these facilities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: We took it back in two days' time, that part there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, were you in a position to hear the fighting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: When I was present there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, let's move on to July 1993 and the end of this month. Was there any large-scale fighting in your area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, we will now show you another photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is 3760. The usher will place it on the ELMO, immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, meanwhile, I inform you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Four minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Four minutes. Okay, that is fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you can see this photograph which we examined in part earlier on. To the right there is the serpentine form of a beige or brownish path. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness showed to this "S" shaped path, an S-shaped mark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does this represent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: This is the trench that was used by the enemy side. It goes from the bottom from these houses and reaches as far as this peak here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, the trees that we can see there, did that correspond to the edge of the forest that you indicated to us a minute ago near to the hill where we have elevation number 906?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes. Elevation 906, it's somewhere there. You can't see it on the photograph, but it is behind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, at the bottom of the photograph and towards the left corner we can see a cylindrical structure with a grey top. Can you see it? Can you point to it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness did so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, slightly to the right of this object we can see darker traces on the ground which join up with a house. A little further down, a little further --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you see a line, further up. Further up, Witness. Can you see a light house? Further up. Further up. Even further.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, further up, please. Go up. No.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Stop. To the left now. To the left. Laterally. Further up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see a zone there? Can you see a darker land zone there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: This light area, this represents trenches. It was the second line of defence which I drew a minute ago on the map. That is the second line of defence. You can see the trenches here and this is where they were, it went in this direction. I don't think this house was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The witness pointed to a lighter land areas in the field, in the foreground and slightly to the right of the cylindrical object. We can remove this photograph from the screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that you went to the village of Mrkovici to sleep, to have a rest. Why did you do this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, because I had a family house in Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You said it was there. What has happened to it now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: The house was set on fire two years ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did that, can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is this relevant to hear about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, what is the relevance? If this could be -- may I ask you, Mr. DP53, do you understand or speak any English and/or French?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we could ask the witness to take his earphones off. Mr. Stamp, I take it that the witness cannot follow the English or French, but if you would have any hesitation then --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. It is relevant in that it doesn't, in fact, concern the events that concern Mr. -- General Galic and the events that concern his responsibility. It has to do with the proceedings itself. We have many witnesses who are afraid of measures. If they came to testify in open session, they would tell us we are afraid for our families, our property, et cetera. And we have a witness here who tells us that his house was set on fire two years ago. And I think that it is necessary to provide you with such information. You should be aware of this, to be aware of what the witnesses are afraid of. This is not something that we imagine, but it is something that they may really fear on a daily basis, since they -- their people and friends who have experienced such things. That's why it is relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am a bit surprised that this has not been -- has been -- has been one of the reasons why you applied for protective measures. But if that would demonstrate to us clearly, but I have no objection. Please, the Chamber will allow you to put this question, but in this limited sense. Mr. Usher, could you please ask the witness to put his headphones on again. Mr. DP53, the question was whether you know who put your family house to fire? Please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't personally know that, but the house is in the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and probably --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please move to your next subject, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to Mrkovici and you said that this was almost on a weekly basis, did you ever have the opportunity of seeing an artillery unit of any kind which had heavy -- large-calibre mortars, 120-millimetre mortars?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat that answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the answer, Mr. DP53, because it was not heard by the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't see Mrkovici. It was an inhabited place.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions, Mr. President. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Mr. Stamp, is the Prosecution ready to cross-examine the witness? Mr. DP53, you will now be examined by counsel for the Prosecution. Cross-examined by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know an officer in your brigade by the name of Cvetkovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Perhaps the interpreters might help me it is spelt C-V-E-T-K-O-V-I-C with a half banana over the "C" if that could be translated to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't know. I didn't know him. I've heard about him, but I didn't know him personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who the artillery commander for your brigade or for the Mrkovici area was, if there was one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you never saw any artillery or mortar positions in the region of Mrkovici; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No, I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what it sounds like when a mortar fires or an artillery gun fires? Do you know the sound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: You can hear it, but not that much, only if you are in the vicinity, but not if you are further away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that is not what I asked you. I asked you if you know the sound of the firing, and I presume your answer is you do, know the sound.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there is a problem with the transcript, at least with the French transcript. One of the interpreters that I have been listening to didn't hear the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you to repeat that last answer and to speak clearly and loud to the microphone, because the interpreters who have to translate everything you say so that we can understand it, they have some difficulties in hearing you. So could you please repeat your last answer. The last answer by Mr. Stamp is whether you knew the sound and then you answered. Could you repeat that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It depended on what was involved. You could hear the sound of heavy artillery, but further away, but the sound of a mortar couldn't be heard at a distance when a shell is fired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It is not entirely repetition of your previous answer, but it is at least a more extensive answer. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, from about how far could you hear when an artillery gun is fired?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, yet again, the problem concerns the competence of the person, that's the issue. And in accordance with the general rules, we must determine whether the witness is in a position to comment on such matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In his previous answer the witness did say anything about distances from which you could hear, so the next question is a logical one that follows. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear my last question and understand it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, not that well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to know from about how far you can hear an artillery gun being fired from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Perhaps a few kilometers, a couple of kilometers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about how far would you say that you -- well, let me ask you this: While you were at home in Mrkovici or on the line where you were stationed, did you ever hear artillery guns or mortars being fired from the region, the area where the village of Mrkovici is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Not from mortars because they probably don't make such a sound, when you fire from mortars. But when heavy artillery was used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We don't want to waste time so I am going to try to understand what you are saying. Basically, I take it you have never heard the sound of a mortar being fired from the area of the village of Mrkovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have heard -- and I am asking -- have you heard artillery guns being fired from the area of the village of Mrkovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Fire was never opened if there wasn't an infantry attack. So such times there was fire coming from all directions. So it was very difficult to determine what was being fired from because the sound is such, and the layout of the terrain is such that it is difficult to determine what weapons are being used. It is difficult to determine whether it is a shell that is falling or whether it is a shooting, and fire was never opened in peaceful conditions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's get back to the question I asked you. Can you tell us whether or not you have ever heard artillery guns being fired in the area of the village of Mrkovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Not from the area of Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the question has been answered, but I wanted to say that the witness had said in his previous response that it was almost impossible to determine where fire was coming from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The witness has now answered the question, so, Mr. Stamp, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree or disagree with the statement that in the year proceeding or the 12-month time proceeding February 1994, 30.000 or more rounds, artillery and mortar rounds had been fired from the area of Mrkovici into the city?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would not agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness has answered on two occasions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... before you now, he has not answered the question just put by Mr. Stamp. He has answered questions about whether he ever heard something, that's a personal observation, that's how I understand the question and that question has been answered. And now something else is put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, what I wanted to say, but perhaps the witness should take his headphones off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please take your headphones off for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I wanted to say, the question, as it was put, how can we know whether 30.000 shells were fired? What's the extent of human memory? How can we ask whether someone can remember the number of shells fired? It is a good example of a question that is almost impossible to answer. That's what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's a -- it's a question, if you understood the question to be exactly 30.000, I would fully agree with you that spending your days in counting every single shell would not be possible. But that's not how I understood the question. I understood the question to be that in a huge number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question to you was whether you have any knowledge, whether you heard it by yourself or -- yes, please. Mr. Stamp put the question to you whether you were aware that in 1993, almost during the whole year, a huge number of artillery and mortar rounds were fired from Mrkovici into the city? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not from Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From any other place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The artillery was only used if our lines were attacked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stamp, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the President asked if you know of artillery shells being fired into the city from any other place but Mrkovici, do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never saw it and you never heard it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Were you posted on the ridge at Spicasta Stijena or at the fortress that you call Kula -- Mala Kula or in the area of both places?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, at all places, from Mala Kula to Velika Kula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said -- so how often were you at Velika Kula?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, the disposition changed every ten days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you'd be -- can I take it do you mean that you would be at Velika Kula for 10 days and then at Mala Kula for another 10 days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sometimes you would be on the sharpstone ridge for 10 days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far did you say Velika Kula is from Mala Kula, as the crow flies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: About 2 and a half kilometers. 2.500 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said there was firing from the -- or may I ask you: You said that -- is it your evidence that there was firing from the barracks in the Bakija area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you return the fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Not personally, but it depended who was on the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: But immediately just next to the barracks there was fire opened from a mortar, so with infantry weapons you can't really respond. It is a lot of distance between.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when I asked you earlier did you return the fire to the Bakija area, and you said "yes" well, I have it as "yes" in answer, you really meant no, you didn't return the fire to the Bakija area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: The barracks in the Bakija area where it is, it's from our positions the distance is about 1.200 metres, approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't return the fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any other VRS military unit try to fire at those mortars or that mortar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: They tried to fire into -- at near the command of the battalion there were mortars. And we used them in the case of their attack. So we would inform the commander of the battalion that we were attacked and then they would undertake further steps to protect us by these mortars, when we were attacked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the command of the battalion would return the fire with mortars; is that what your answer is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Not the command, but next to the command attached to the command of the battalion there was a unit. I don't know what they are called, what it's called, but they had mortars, the unit had mortars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of mortars did this unit have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see them. I never saw them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What calibre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: I never saw them, but I believe that they had -- no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You believe they had what, what calibres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: I think they had 82 and 100 -- 120-millimetres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where these mortars were located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No. That was somewhere behind, somewhere further up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "behind" you mean behind your lines as you faced Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Behind the settlement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Behind which settlement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have upper Mrkovici or --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Somewhere further behind, somewhere further up. Yes. I lived in the upper part of Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how far did you live from these mortar batteries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: I don't know where they were stationed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you know it is somewhere further up and you lived further up; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No. I was in the upper part of Mrkovici and I don't know where they were stationed, these...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you become aware that there were mortar batteries there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well in the event of attack, we asked, that was through the company commander, we requested assistance, and then he then informed further on to the higher command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that there were mortars, as you put it further behind, somewhere further up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: They were probably somewhere because they were not there in the sector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, we are close to the time where we usually have a break. If you would find a suitable moment, please inform me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is an appropriate moment, suitable moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will then have a break until five minutes to 6.00

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before the witness is brought in, there was an issue raised earlier today as to the propriety of putting to the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We discussed it and as a matter of fact the Chamber intended to give some more guidance to the parties at a later stage, that will be next Monday. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To give you some guidance, the majority of the Chamber does not oppose against to putting to a witness, even if that would be putting to a witness a potential involvement in crimes committed. One of the other things is the way it is done. You can do it in different ways. And the Chamber is -- would be reluctant to accept that it is done in such a way that the witness might feel less free to give answers to questions. So it is for the majority of the Chamber, it is still a concern, the way it is done, but the majority of the Chamber does not oppose against putting it to a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Vaso Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a member of your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you met him here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you discussed his testimony with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many members were there in your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, the manpower situation changed because it would happen that there would be many injured. But it was about 100. It would be 110, 90, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many would normally be stationed or posted at the ridge called Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Depended on the people who were on disposal. It would be from 7 to 10. If there were many who were wounded, many who were not in the company, then, of course, it would be fewer. Of course, if there was an attack, then everyone from the company would come to the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was there an observation post on that ridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it on the edge of the ridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No. Below the edge of the ridge their forces were, and because this part could be seen from Sedrenik, it couldn't be there because it was constantly fired at, so you couldn't go right to the edge of the ridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me try to understand you. You couldn't place it at the edge of the ridge because it could be seen from Sedrenik; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I understand you to mean that you had to place it somewhere where it could not be seen from Sedrenik, and that is why it was placed behind the edge of the ridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, it would be slightly withdrawn from the actual edge of the ridge. It would be more inward. Because the rock or the stone doesn't go right steeply, it goes up and then up to a height and then it goes downwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it would be in that position, I take it, because it could not be seen from Sedrenik in that position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the position where it was put, could it see into Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, that one part that I drew there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness answered, but bearing in mind that there was a previous answer given it would be good to clarify the question because the witness said that one section could not be seen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That part that I drew could be seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps if you ask for a clarification do not explain why the clarification is needed, because that might guide the witness, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. So let's try to avoid whatever influence to be put on the answers of the witness by the party who called the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was in a position where you could see part of Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the part of Sedrenik that you could see from that observation post could also see the observation post or the place where the observation post was; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what position could you see the barracks at Bakija?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: That barracks could be seen from the observation point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it possible to fire in the direction of the barracks from the observation point? I want you to understand the question clearly. I am not asking you if it was possible to fire at the barracks itself, but the direction of the barracks from the observation point.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: It was possible to fire but there was no effect because it was far too far away to fire with infantry weapons all the way to the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. But the village or the community of Sedrenik which is closer to the observation point than the barracks, was it possible to fire into Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: It was possible to fire, but again, there is a great distance. There is no effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Along that line into Sedrenik, have you ever seen civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I wanted to have a clarification. Perhaps we should ask the witness not to answer so quickly. Perhaps the witness could remove his earphones, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please take off your earphones. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. The reason why I am objecting is the following: We have the words "line into Sedrenik" so I don't know whether this is a hypothetical line, which would have been a target line or a firing line or are we talking about a defence line. If we are talking about the line of defence, then we should know that there are three of them so which one is it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Along that line into Sedrenik and as far as I am aware there was no line of defence ever drawn by the witness along which you could fire into Sedrenik. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. I will clarify that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We were talking earlier about your line of vision from your observation post to the barracks of Bakija, Witness. Would you agree --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: I didn't hear it from the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you put your question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your evidence that you could see the barracks at Bakija from your observation post on Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And between those barracks and your observation post there is the community of Sedrenik; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the community of Sedrenik, have you ever seen civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No, except in the beginning in 1992, I already told you, nobody knew who was a civilian, who was soldier. There were no uniforms. We didn't have them; they didn't have them. But later on, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1993 did you see civilians in Sedrenik at all? Did you see any person in Sedrenik --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The interpreters have not heard your last answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which part, I am sorry. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any person in Sedrenik at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No, not even the army. Because the communicating trenches were dug up, which they used to walk through, so it was hard to see anyone, when they would come to the positions, when they would be leaving the positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I just want to make it clear. In the entire year 1993, you saw no person in Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No. We didn't see any civilians anywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. In 1993, did you see any person, whether it be civilian or military, in Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No. In 1993 we had several attacks among others. It is the first time that I was wounded, in 1993. So there was frequent fighting and in the event of an attack you couldn't really watch down there any more. Because we had to withdraw to this line of the defence. If you want me to illustrate, I can, what the sharpstone rock feature looked like. It looks like these desks you have before you. So it would be -- there would be a plateau and then it would go vertical and we would be behind there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it, therefore, there was no need for you to use infantry weapons except in case of an attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes. We didn't use them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you see the trenches from your -- could you see the enemy trenches from your trenches on Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please take your headphones off.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I want to have a precision because the witness showed us very clearly several lines of defence, and it could make a difference as to what we are thinking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stamp, I think it would be useful to perhaps be a bit more precise in that respect. I would not say that the question is inadmissible, but could easily lead to a lot of confusion. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were posted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First the witness should have his earphones on. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am sorry to ask the witness to remove his earphone, because I would really like the witness to answer the question I asked. And if I may with your leave --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As I said, the question was not inadmissible, the previous question --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Perhaps I rephrase it. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You showed us on a photograph and on a map what you say were the lines of defence. Now my question is this: From your positions in Spicasta Stijena or Mala Kula, could you see any of them during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: From the sharpstone we were able to look or to see the second and the third line that I -- as I drew that on the map where from the second and the third line of defence could be seen. The first line. That's just according to the information, and I know where they were firing at us from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you fire towards these lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Only in the event of their attack or some acts of provocation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you saw an enemy soldiers armed anywhere, would you fire at that soldier even if there was no attack going on at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: It depends on which sector. If it is in the immediate vicinity of the defence line, normally I would fire because that's how sabotage groups were approaching trying to infiltrate without an attack. Normally in the sector of defence, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you saw an enemy soldier within the range of your gun, would you fire at him, anywhere within the range of your gun, I am asking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is because you are obeying orders not to fire except if there was an attack; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that apply throughout the indictment -- well, did that apply throughout the period August 1992 to September 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in the course of your military duties when you had to fire, where did you fire to, which area did you fire towards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: It depends on the trench that I was in at that moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Whether --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the trenches on Spicasta Stijena which areas did you fire towards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: From the trenches on the Spicasta Stijena you cannot see anything except that slope in front. It is only from the observation post that you would see part of Sedrenik, but from the trenches you would only see that part of Spicasta Stijena which isn't vertical. And there is also another bit which goes around Trebevic, the transit road around Trebevic. Just like here, from here, I can't see what is behind there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All I am asking is simply where would you fire to when you were in those trenches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, if we fired from the trenches, that would mean that there would come already to the rock and they would be firing mortars or some other weapons. So the distance would be 20 metres. If they were using hand held launchers and other weapons then we would be firing at them and they would be firing in front of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP53, I think that you have to listen very careful to the questions of Mr. Stamp and try to understand them and to answer them as precise as possible. The question was where you were firing at from those trenches, and I did hear your answer. You said they were already close, if we had to fire from those trenches. Then where you -- when you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but that's the direction towards Sedrenik, downwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, please proceed, Mr. Stamp. I will not interfere any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your answer, are you saying that from the trenches you would be firing downwards towards Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: In that direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Would you be firing from the trenches downwards towards Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes, in the event of an attack because it was from that direction their troops came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would be firing down the slopes of the ridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I just get something quite clear in my own mind. Your trenches were how far behind this edge or ridge that faces Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: 15 to 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do I take it from your evidence that there was a hump at the edge of the ridge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Just like here, just like here in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. You are indicating the box with the monitor in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is my understanding correct that to fire down the slopes towards Sedrenik you would have to get out of your trenches and go to the edge where there is that hump like the box with the monitor in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes, but in the event of firing it was impossible to get out there because we would be fired at from below with the weapons, so you couldn't get out on there. And otherwise, in peace conditions you could never get to the very edge. You would get out once and never again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So from where would you fire down the slopes towards Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: We didn't fire down the slope, but only from the trenches in the event of their attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at any time -- I am sorry. Did you at any time see screens and barricades in the area of Sedrenik? And by that I mean anti-sniping screens and barricades in the community of Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: They were in the trenches and the communicating trenches where their troops walked, and that could be seen from the observation post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: With your leave, Mr. President, Your Honours, could my learned colleague proceed with the rest of the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, is my recollection correct that you were not present during the examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It is, Mr. President. I was following the evidence from a monitor and preparing some material in relation to cross-examination. If your concern is that I am not familiar with it, I have not only followed it, but I have also read printouts of the LiveNote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I think that's very peculiar because we lost something here. If Mr. Ierace was all this time following it from his TV screen and reading the LiveNote, why wasn't he here? I believe that the rule is such that there is no cross-examination by the counsel unless he was there all the time, unless he was partially informed elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The majority decision of the Chamber is that Mr. Ierace is allowed to cross-examine the witness up to the very moment where it appears to the Chamber that he is not fully aware of what happened during examination-in-chief, just as we allowed the Defence to cross-examine the witness even if counsel had not been present during the examination-in-chief, up to the moment where it appeared that counsel was not informed about what happened during the examination-in-chief. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. Ierace:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you told us that from the trenches you could not see, that is from your trenches, you could not see the first line of trenches of the defence; and you've told us that the observation post was positioned back behind the ridge. How then were you able to make sure that enemy troops did not make their way from their front line trench up the slope?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: If they went to the stone feature, they would attack us, they would fire at us with Zoljas. That is a distance of about 20 to 30 metres. That's how we lost those two trenches on two occasions. When they were on the sharpstone feature itself, they would start firing at us. And after that, they would enter the trenches. And this is how we lost those trenches at the sharpstone feature on a couple of occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would appreciate it if Mr. Ierace would follow this on the monitor, could tell us whether the witness used the term "back behind the ridge" because I don't think that is exactly what he said in Serbian. Could we be provided would the exact quote, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, not in Serbian, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, to save time, my recollection is that one of the questions that made that clear was a question asked by Mr. Stamp as to how far back from the edge were the trenches to which the witness replied, 15 to 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but that is not the observation post, is it? That is the trenches. That's not the same, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, I accept that, Mr. President, but I maintain that the witness did in any event say that the trenches were behind the ridge line. It was in the last period of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I am going to read the question and the answer. "Was there an observation post on that ridge? "Yes. "Was it on the edge of the ridge? "No, below the edge of the ridge." It is line 64 -- page 64, line 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I accept that. Although I -- my recollection is that there were questions about the ridge being -- I am sorry, the trenches being behind the ridge, perhaps I can clarify that and continue with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I would rather first clarify it for ourselves, Mr. Ierace, because we allowed you to cross-examine under a certain condition.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, page 73 line 3 the question: "Can I just get something quite clear in my mind. Your trenches were how far behind this edge or ridge that faces Sedrenik?" Answer: "15 to 20 metres."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said page 73, line -- I haven't found it yet. You said page 73 line --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: 3 to 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your question to which an objection was made was about an observation post, if I am correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The question is: "You told us that from the trenches that you could not see, that is from your trenches, you could not see the first line of trenches of the defence." That is the first proposition, which in my recollection is sound in terms of the evidence. I read on from that: "And you've told us that the observation post was positioned back behind the ridge." And I think the passage read out by His Honour Judge Nieto-Navia establishes that. Reading on: "How then were you able to make sure that enemy troops did not make their way from their front line trench up the slope?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is not exactly the same. Behind and below is not exactly the same. The Chamber would prefer that Mr. Stamp continues to cross-examine the witness. And of course you may - as we allow the Defence to always - assist each other by consultation. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If I may just have a moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I just want to point out that I will need five minutes after this intervention in order to put certain other questions. And unfortunately I won't be here on Monday. If this could be taken into account, I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I will proceed, Mr. President, quite speedily. Further cross-examination by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suggest to you, Witness, that there were anti-sniping barriers put up at the intersections in Sedrenik; is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did troops of your unit shoot at any motor vehicle of any description in the area of Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say, Witness, whether or not troops from your units positioned at Spicasta Stijena fired at any person in Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No, they didn't. Only in the event of an attack, then they would open fire in the direction of the attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that from your personal knowledge that none of your troops at Spicasta Stijena fired at civilians or persons in Sedrenik, is that from your personal knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that sometimes you were posted at Velika Kula 2 and a half kilometers from Mala Kula. How far is that from Spicasta Stijena? Or may I rephrase. How far is Velika Kula from Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: I didn't say half a kilometre from Mala Kula. I said 2 kilometers from Mala Kula. That's a mistake. And it is about between 700 and 800 metres from Spicasta Stijena going towards the east.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: In the occasional 10 days that you were posted at Velika Kula can you say from your own personal knowledge whether or not soldiers on Spicasta Stijena fired at civilians in Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, on the basis of what I myself know, I don't believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you don't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, I can't claim this for certain for that period, but I am not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suggest to you, Witness, that members of the units, the Sarajevo Romanija Corps units posted at Spicasta Stijena fired on civilians in Sedrenik; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suggest to you that artillery guns and Howitzers positioned in the area of Mrkovici regularly fired into Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am saying that that's not the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness has answered that question. I don't know whether there is any specific need --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Too late.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suggest to you, Witness, that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or I would ask firstly, can you remember if there was a truce in effect on the 17th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: I can't remember that because there was no truce. We were attacked then and that is the first time I was wounded. So maybe there was one in force, but not in reality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the date you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: 17th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: In a trench next to the sharpstone feature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you wounded? By what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: It was a bullet which fragmented.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the time of day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, the attack lasted throughout the day, and that was about half past 12.00. 12.30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I suggest to you, Witness, that there was no attack that day in your area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: I have proof.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: I am saying that I was wounded then and the effects of this wound are still visible now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is not an answer to my question. I am suggesting to you that there was no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, isn't that clear what the witness says.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please move to your next subject.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you were wounded by a bullet. Where was this firing coming from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: On that day I was in a trench between the Spicasta Stijena and Mala Kula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the firing coming from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: It was right in front of us, since their trenches in that area were 80 metres in front of us. The area in between is a forested area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say how many troops were involved in that attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: It is difficult to say, but there were quite a few troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can give me an approximation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well over a hundred, for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin. If it would be possible to finish today with this witness, that would be preferable, but let's see how much time you will need.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will be very quick, Mr. President. Thank you. Re-examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, if you could just answer the questions by saying yes or no, if the questions allow you to do this, we would appreciate it. You mentioned the 17th of April, you said that that's when you were wounded. Do you know how many cartridge clips you emptied on that day, approximately, in the course of the combat?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is not a proper way to ask a question. But it is already in. Did you fire, how many did you fire, it could have been done like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it the description given by the witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we opened fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, now the witness is answering the questions of Mr. Stamp. It would be the proper questions on the other hand. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. I was assuming that there was a fighting. Witness, if you did open fire, how many cartridge clips did you personally empty on that day, on the 17th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: He repeats -- counsel --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember exactly, but six or seven for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... for the purposes of the record. That type of question is highly improper and cause the witness to put to the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the proper way of doing is first to find out whether there was any firing and then of course the next question would have been whether the witness fired and whether he participated or whether others were fired. So please proceed, but keep in mind --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, gladly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you had emptied about six cartridge clips. Do you know whether your comrades in arm also opened fire in the course of this attack; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, after I had been wounded I was taken away from the lines and the fighting continued until the evening, so, yes, for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. Cartridge clip or the sort of cartridge clips that you had, how many shots does it contain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Thirty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Did the other men possess the same type of weapons; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you were asked about returning fire and you said that in general you wouldn't shoot because you were ordered only to return fire, only to open fire in return. You said this page 66 and page 70. Do you remember having said that; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, as you said that, am I to understand that you were ordered, that you received orders, and who did you receive these orders from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: We received these orders from our immediate superior, that is to say the company commander. These orders would arrive very often. We were told to save ammunition and not open fire unless we were attacked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the nature of these orders and how often were you given such orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, we received such orders as new troops would often arrive -- usually when new troops would arrived these orders would be issued and repeated to the others. I don't know, every 15 or 20 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did these orders also cover the issue of protecting civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes, these orders always stated that civilians shouldn't be fired at.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That doesn't arise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I take it --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Also very leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, this is, I think, the 25th or 30th or sometimes there is no objection, but now there is an objection. It is justified. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will move on to another subject. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said you would be five minutes --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm -- I'll -- I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke about Mrkovici earlier on in relation to the upper part of Mrkovici, and in relation to the artillery, do you remember speaking about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I am not sure I heard your question very well in the Serbian language. Could you confirm the following: Did you ever see any kind of artillery unit in the upper part of Mrkovici; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you said that there were mortars, was this an assumption, is that how I am to understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: There weren't any in the area of Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will now move on to the issue of attacks. You spoke about attacks launched against you, you spoke about lines and trenches. The line, the barracks was discussed and my question is a dual question: Was fire opened from so-called civilian houses, that is the first part of my question; and the second part of my question is: What could the naked eye see at a distance of 800 metres, approximately?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Those --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, I warned you a couple of times, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. And now you are asking questions so I will --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was just about to give a decision on the objection, but since you have no more questions. Judge -- first of all, I have to ask the technical booth and the interpreters whether we could finish? I think it is just a matter of a few questions. If you would agree then we could prevent the witness having to stay here for all the weekend.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No problem for the interpreters, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I thank you for your cooperation. I think it is important for you as well Mr. DP53, Judge El Mahdi has a question. Questioned by the Court: JUDGE EL MAHDI: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] With the assistance of the usher, could we place exhibit -- the Defence exhibit, the two photographs on the ELMO, yes. Witness, in your opinion, was this photograph taken from positions which were under your control, that is to say under the control of Serbian troops?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] In that case, where was this photograph taken from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: In front of those positions which were under the control of the BH Army. You can see the trench that they used to approach. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes. You want to say the trenches that one can see in the right part of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] And it seems to me that this photograph was taken from an elevated position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes, but on this side of the elevation they also had their positions, that is at a distance of about between 50 and 100 metres. That is the distance between our positions and their positions. Not at the sharpstone feature itself, this is to the right. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes, in order to understand you correctly, you are saying that this photo was taken from positions which were under the control of the enemy side, that is to say the BH side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] If you can remember this -- Madam Registrar, the map, please. You traced the line of vision on the map, the line of vision from your positions; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] And you also marked a line which goes beyond, which is to your left, and that was the first line of the enemy party. So it was to your left from the position that you are looking at the map. If I have understood you correctly, you were not in a position to see these trenches, this was not possible; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes. Your line of vision, if I have understood you correctly, and if I have understood the traces correctly, you couldn't go further to the left of the line that you have traced from the red circle at the bottom and right up to the barracks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: But this part between the sharpstone feature and the small fortress, the layout of the terrain is such that there is a canyon there and it is covered by forest. You see the elevation point 906 here. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes, but it was possible for you to see them then, to see those trenches there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: These ones here, yes, between the small fortress and -- JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes, to the right of the line, at least the trenches.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have got a few questions. Could the witness be shown the photograph P3756. Yes. Are you able to indicate on this photograph with the pointer where the trenches are you just described in the other photograph that looks down? Do you remember that you told us the "S" line more or less was trenches of the opposite forces. Could you indicate on the photograph in front of you where these trenches exactly are.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Here. You can still here the communicating here, where the trenches were, where they were. So just here. On the very edge above the area, and then it went down here, this way, through the canyon up to here, right here. So the communicating trench went down below the stone, the rock. So in this little part here of the wood, both their trenches and our trenches were there, here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Except that on the map it is very small and in real life there is 200 metres difference -- distance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could then the photograph P3760 be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: While that is being done, may I just inquire of the court if there would be no objection to him marking that line that he just showed on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is the document that is already in evidence and we cannot mark on exhibits that are already in evidence. We would change them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But before I show you the other photograph, you told us a lot about what was on the ridge, your trenches being behind the ridge. Were there any trees that would give any cover to you on that ridge? I mean, just on the edge.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes, there were, but when the attacks took place from their side, those trees as it could be seen on the photographs, those trees had dried up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So they were not there any more. On from what moment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: The beginning, there were many of them and later on, fewer and fewer. Because they were drying up from the bullets that they were being hit by and from other weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you now please look at photograph P3760. Could you again indicate where you saw the trenches of the other part on that photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: These trenches here below the sharpstone rock. That's the first line here. And in the wood itself in this valley between small and large fort, that could be seen with the naked eye because there was 100 metres distance between them and us. On this left-hand side, this other part of the photograph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me first ask you about that trench. You just indicated the "S" line more or less brownish approximately in the middle of the right-hand side of the wooded area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you see soldiers of the opposite parties in those trenches.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: We couldn't not in this communicating trench because we didn't see this section, just further up where the trenches were because they are further up some 100 metres further up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I now take you back to the down in the valley you were asked about a cylindrical object. Can you find that. Down on the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Yes, here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then a bit more to the right where there is a house, there you said were there trenches in that dark area near that house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: They could not be seen but the communicating trench could be even seen now, that it existed, but this part here, to the left, the second part of the photograph, you could see the communicating trenches very clearly from our observation post between the houses. But this part here, we couldn't see, this part here we couldn't see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How would you know that these trenches weren't there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, we had the counter-intelligence information. Because part of the Serbs who left the city then they would transmit this information, those people who stayed down there in the beginning of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What did they tell you? Did they tell it to you or did they tell it to anyone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No. That was -- they would transmit this to the command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and what did your commander tell you then about these trenches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, he would tell us where it was approximately because we knew the terrain. He would tell us where they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How did he describe that to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, important -- referring to important facilities that were in the vicinity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. How would he describe where these facilities were, especially those trenches you just indicated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: These communicating trenches from the house, since we knew about this area here, we would know some of the inhabitants from these houses. So we would have reference points among these houses, for instance, around here, this house here or the owner of the house, I knew what their name was. So that's how I would know. So what would be said was in the direction of such-and-such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That white house, who owned that house that you just pointed at? That house you just indicated, yes? No, no, the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: This. Not this one. This one wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you give me the names of those who owned these houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: We called it Kodismanovici [phoen] Probably that who the owners were Osman -- Osman or Osmanovi -- Osman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You knew the owners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Personally, no. Personally I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have another question about tanks. You said something about tanks or a tank. I don't know. You told us that you saw the tank or tanks at two positions, at the Ciglana tunnel. Do you remember when you saw the tank there, one time, several times?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Well, I saw it on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From where did you see it? Where were you when you saw it? Always at the same spot or different spots?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: Not that part with the area in Ciglana could be seen from another part west from the small fort. That part at Ciglana can be seen from that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are west from that fortress? Was there an observation post as well as that point or?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP53
utterances.text: No, there was a trench there, below the fort to the right-hand side, our trench in the wood. But from there you could see all the way west or north-western part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. These were my questions. This then concludes your testimony in this court, Mr. DP53. I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague. We all know that it is a very long distance for you and I would like to thank you for answering all the questions of both parties and of the Bench. And I wish you have a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you then escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn, but not after I have thanked thoroughly the interpreters and the technical booth. I must say I feel a bit guilty where we stopped early yesterday. It seems that if the Chamber is taking revenge, I hope that you accept that that was not our intention. We will adjourn until next Monday at 9.00 in the morning, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
